transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Customer billing services, my name is Arthur.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Arthur, my name is Oliver Wright. I received my monthly landline bill this morning and there is a sixty-five-pound charge for three calls to a premium rate directory enquiry number 118 434, but nobody in our household made these calls: we only ever use Google or telephone contacts!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Oliver. If I understand correctly, your landline bill shows an unexpected sixty-five-pound charge for directory enquiry calls to 118 434 that no one in your household made. Before we inspect the itemized call log, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 54 Church Road, Cheltenham, GL51 7SN, security PIN 2291, landline number 01242 559102.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Oliver, that confirms your account details. What specific dates and call times are listed for those three 118 calls?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They are listed on September 12th at 2:15 PM, September 14th at 4:30 PM, and September 18th at 11:00 AM, each billed at over twenty pounds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query the British Telecom wholesale interconnect billing gateway?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Oliver. The wholesale interconnect records show physical dialing origin from the local subscriber loop on 01242 559102.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why would the wholesale records claim the calls originated from our loop when no one in the house dialed 118 434?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wholesale telephony billing relies on automated Calling Line Identification signaling generated by the local master socket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you refund the sixty-five pounds and block all premium rate 118 numbers on our telephone line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If people in your household dial premium directory enquiry numbers to find local tradesmen, you have to pay for the connection service.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I live alone with my dog! My dog does not dial directory enquiries! Why are you accusing my household of lying?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am stating the operational reality of certified public switched telephone network billing records.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I want an official dispute raised with your fraud investigation team right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Dispute forms can be registered on our corporate billing system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you still there? The line was completely silent for over thirty seconds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I was retrieving the national premium rate regulatory dispute tariff sheet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please apply an immediate bar on all premium rate numbers right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously premium rate directory numbers operate on third-party tariff bands set by the phone-paid services regulator.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't care who sets the tariff band; I want premium calls barred from my line!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oliver speaking, I am a pensioner on a fixed state pension, and sixty-five pounds is my entire heating budget for two weeks! S-Net taking sixty-five pounds from my current account for fraudulent directory calls will leave me choosing between heating and eating this month! I am terrified, sick with anxiety, and desperate for your help!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how deeply distressing and frightening this sixty-five-pound charge is on a fixed pension, Oliver, especially when you are worried about covering heating and food this month. You should never be placed in financial distress over disputed calls, and I will place an immediate bar on premium calls and submit this dispute to our billing review team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you credit the sixty-five pounds back to my account balance today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Premium rate charges over fifty pounds require formal review by our wholesale interconnect carrier before credit can be released.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long does that wholesale interconnect review take?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wholesale interconnect carriers respond to formal billing challenges within ten to fourteen working days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ten to fourteen days?! My pension direct debit will be collected this Friday!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can place a temporary collection hold on the disputed sixty-five-pound balance so your bank account is not debited this Friday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will protect my pension this week. Please apply that direct debit collection hold immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The collection stay has been applied to invoice reference INV-88192-O.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: INV-88192-O, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am also activating our Premium Rate Call Barring feature on your exchange line free of charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Arthur? Arthur, are you still there? Hello? Why does your phone line keep going completely dead?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am here, Oliver. The exchange switchboard confirmed the premium rate bar has been locked onto line 01242 559102.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So no one can ever dial premium numbers from our telephone again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct, any outbound call beginning with 09, 118, or international premium prefixes will be rejected by the dial tone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me security for the future, but what about the sixty-five-pound refund?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The dispute ticket is logged under reference DISP-440192-P.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: DISP-440192-P, noted.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will receive written notification of the wholesale review outcome by post within fourteen days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the final credit is not approved today and I will have to wait for the post?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just making sure our premises records match perfectly: that was 14 Montpellier Terrace, wasn't it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 14 Montpellier Terrace, Cheltenham.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Oliver, the dispute submission is formally queued for review.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am relieved my heating money is safe for Friday, but disappointed the credit could not be settled immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our corporate policies dictate carrier arbitration for third-party operator billings.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood. I will wait for the letter in the post.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other aspect of your landline account I can assist you with today, Oliver?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Arthur, that is all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
